item.title: Assembly Drill 2026-11-14: crackme
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64.
``` check: mov eax, ecx xor eax, 0x5A rol eax, 4 cmp eax, 0x50000006 jne fail mov eax, 1 ret fail: xor eax, eax ret ```
`rol eax, 4` rotates left by 4 bits: bits shifted out of the top re-enter at the bottom (unlike `shl`, nothing is lost). Which unsigned `x` (ecx) makes `check` return 1?
---
**Answer:** `x = 0x6500005A` (1694498906)
1. Work backwards: undo `rol 4` with `ror 4` (rotate right). 0x50000006 → the low nibble `6` wraps to the top, giving 0x65000000. 2. `xor` is its own inverse: 0x65000000 ^ 0x5A = 0x6500005A. 3. Check forwards: 0x6500005A ^ 0x5A = 0x65000000; rotating left 4 moves the top `6` round to the bottom → 0x50000006. A `shl` would have dropped that `6`, so the wrap is the whole point.
